0.description: Fill colour, any CSS colour (e.g. `#a1531a`). Default cycles a palette.
Outline colour, any CSS colour. Default white.

properties.description:
Ordered rules. For each feature, the first rule whose `source` is the collection it came from
and whose `match` (if any) applies decides how it is drawn; a feature no rule claims is not
drawn. A non-empty list replaces the built-in rules entirely.

Top-level collection of the document to classify, e.g. `solids`, `parcels`, `faces`,
`rings`, or the derived `surfaces` (shells no solid uses).
Identifier grouping this rule's features, e.g. `parcel-created`.
Groups several kinds under one heading and toggle. Defaults to `kind`.
Human-readable name for this kind, e.g. `Former Tenure`.
How the feature's topology is turned into a shape.

Restricts the rule to features whose property value (or any value, for an array) equals
one of `values`. Values may be literals, CURIEs expanded against the document's own
`@context`, or full URIs; both sides are expanded before comparing.
Dot-separated path into the feature, e.g. `properties.parcelState`.

Where a feature's label comes from: the first of `properties` (dot-separated paths) that
resolves to a non-empty value or to an object with a string `label`, else `fallback`
(default `id`).
Whether the feature is shown when the view opens. Default true.
Defaults merged under every rule; `style` is merged key by key.
Preferred order of kinds, for viewers that list them.

`osm` (default), `ion` (Cesium ion world imagery; needs `ionToken`), or an XYZ tile
template served over https with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}` placeholders.
`ellipsoid` (default, flat) or `ion` (Cesium World Terrain; needs `ionToken`).
Initial view. Without it, the view frames the document's features.
Metres above the ellipsoid.
Degrees clockwise from north. Default 0.
Degrees; negative looks down. Default -45.
Degrees. Default 0.

Cesium ion access token, used only by `ion` imagery or terrain. Never commit one: a
published register injects it at build time from a CI secret. It is visible to anyone
using the viewer, so it must be scoped to `assets:read` and restricted to the register's
domain.
Deepest zoom level the tile server has.
Attribution shown on the globe; required by most tile providers.
